answer_q: How is AI used in eCommerce?
answer: eCommerce businesses use AI to answer product and order questions, process returns and exchanges, triage customer service emails, draft product descriptions, recover abandoned carts and automate back-office tasks such as supplier invoices and stock alerts. Staff handle complex complaints and decisions such as exceptions to returns policy.
body:
Customer service that scales with your sales

Most customer service messages in online retail are the same few questions: where is my order, how do I return this, will it fit, is it in stock? During sales and peak season, volumes jump and response times slip, which costs reviews and repeat customers.

AI answers these questions instantly, around the clock, using live order data and your policies, and passes anything unusual to your team.

Where AI helps online retailers most

Order tracking and “where is my order?”

Customers get instant, accurate order status from your store and courier data by chat or email. See AI chatbot development.

Returns and exchanges

AI checks the order against your returns policy, generates return instructions and flags exceptions for staff approval. See custom AI agents.

Product questions

Sizing, compatibility and stock questions are answered from your catalogue and guides. See LLM, RAG & knowledge-base bots.

Customer service inbox

Emails and social messages are sorted, routine ones answered, and complaints routed to the right person. See AI workflow automation.

Back-office automation

Supplier invoices, stock alerts and daily sales reports run automatically. See document & data processing.

Human-backed AI employees for online retailers

Most online retailers don’t want another tool to supervise. Our AI Employees service builds the AI around your store, then runs it with a dedicated Crenosoft team that learns your services, clients and rules. The AI handles routine work; our reviewers handle anything unusual, around the clock; and decisions that belong to you come to your nominated person with a clear summary. We agree an hours-saved target up front and report against it every month.

Software we connect to

We integrate with Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce and marketplace channels, helpdesks such as Gorgias and Zendesk, Australian courier and shipping platforms with APIs, and accounting software such as Xero.

Consumer law and honest marketing

AI replies follow your published policies and never override consumer guarantees. Under the Australian Consumer Law, customers have rights to repair, replacement or refund for major failures regardless of store policy, and our systems are designed to respect them and pass disputes to staff. The ACCC provides guidance for businesses. Marketing messages respect consent and unsubscribe requests.

Across every project we follow the Privacy Act 1988, the OAIC’s guidance on commercially available AI products and our own Responsible AI Policy.

Preparing for peak season

Black Friday, Christmas and EOFY sales can multiply customer service volume overnight. We recommend setting up AI customer service at least a month before your peak, so it is trained on real questions and tested on live orders. During the sale, the AI absorbs the surge of order-status and returns questions while your team focuses on complaints, VIP customers and anything the AI flags. After peak, the monthly report shows exactly how much volume it handled.

Results we measure for online retailers

Before we build, we record a baseline of how long the work takes and how often it happens. After launch, your monthly report tracks the numbers that matter to online retailers:

  • Customer messages resolved without staff
  • First response time across chat and email
  • Returns processed and exceptions flagged
  • Abandoned carts recovered
  • Peak-season backlog avoided

These figures sit alongside hours saved and accuracy, so you can see exactly what the AI is contributing and where our team is still stepping in.

Smaller stores benefit just as much as large ones. If the owner currently answers every customer email at night, an AI assistant that resolves order-status and sizing questions can give back several hours a week, while making sure complaints and wholesale enquiries still reach a person quickly. As the store grows, the same system scales without extra hires.

Every AI reply is logged against the order, so your team can see exactly what each customer was told before stepping in.

How to get started

  1. Free AI audit: 30 minutes to map your busiest workflows and pick the first opportunity.
  2. Blueprint and fixed quote: what the AI will do, which systems it connects to and the price in AUD.
  3. Build and test: usually two to six weeks, tested on real examples from your store.
  4. Launch and improve: monthly reports on hours saved, accuracy and improvements.

Not sure where to begin? Start with an AI Readiness Assessment, or see how we work locally on our Melbourne AI agency page.
